governanceNotes: D1 batch 44 (2026-09-24): one bounded association edge authored - heterotopic ossification to peripheral neuropathy (rank 1), ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true, and mechanismCategory MECHANICAL_OR_COMPRESSIVE (perineural compression by heterotopic bone). The proposition rests on two independent perineural-compression anchors: the Akhavan 2023 case report and literature review of bony cubital tunnel syndrome, in which heterotopic ossification caused circumferential ulnar-nerve encasement at the elbow with electrodiagnostically confirmed ulnar neuropathy and recovery after excision, and the Daskalakis 2022 case report of elbow heterotopic ossification after distal biceps tendon repair presenting as median-nerve neuropathy. The edge is not raised to causation: the located evidence is case-level plus a narrative literature review without incidence denominators or controlled comparison, perineural heterotopic ossification is rare, and neuropathy in the same patients may arise from concurrent trauma, surgery, or alternative entrapment sites, so no probability estimate is asserted.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Case-level and narrative-review evidence documents that heterotopic bone developing near a peripheral nerve can mechanically encase and compress it: the Akhavan 2023 report describes circumferential ulnar-nerve encasement by heterotopic ossification at the elbow with electrodiagnostically confirmed ulnar neuropathy and functional recovery after excision, and the Daskalakis 2022 report describes elbow heterotopic ossification presenting as median-nerve neuropathy after distal biceps tendon repair - a reproducible lesion-to-compression association that is not an individual causal nexus.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established: the located evidence is case-level plus a narrative literature review without incidence denominators or controlled comparison, perineural heterotopic ossification is rare, and neuropathy in the affected patients may arise from concurrent trauma, the inciting operation, or alternative entrapment sites, so an individual determination requires imaging or operative documentation of the heterotopic bone and its relationship to the affected nerve, electrodiagnostic confirmation of the neuropathy, compatible chronology, and exclusion of other compressive and non-compressive neuropathic causes.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized compression route is described: heterotopic bone forming in the periarticular soft tissues adjacent to a peripheral nerve narrows or obliterates the nerve's anatomic course, and progressive ossification and soft-tissue swelling raise intraneural pressure, impairing axonal transport and myelin perfusion to produce focal demyelinating and ultimately axonal neuropathy - documented in the located reports of ulnar-nerve encasement at the elbow and median-nerve neuropathy after distal biceps repair, with functional recovery following excision - while the case-level evidence base and the high background of concurrent trauma and surgery leave individual attribution hypothesized.
causalMechanism.secondaryVector: Post-traumatic or post-surgical soft-tissue inflammation and fibrosis around the ossification can further tether and compress the nerve, and direct mechanical irritation from the ossific mass during joint motion can add dynamic compression.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The edge asserts an association only: the located evidence is case reports and a narrative literature review documenting perineural encasement and compression by heterotopic bone, without incidence denominators, controlled comparison, or a cohort demonstrating attributable neuropathy, and the affected patients commonly carry concurrent trauma, surgery, and alternative entrapment exposures; an individual claim therefore requires imaging or operative documentation of the heterotopic bone and its nerve relationship, electrodiagnostic confirmation, chronology, and competing-cause review, so no at-least-as-likely-as-not probability is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Imaging or operative documentation of heterotopic ossification (location, extent, relationship to the affected nerve, date); electrodiagnostic confirmation and characterization of the peripheral neuropathy; chronology of the ossification relative to neuropathy onset; documentation of the inciting injury, surgery, or neurologic event; evaluation for alternative or coexisting entrapment sites and for metabolic, toxic, infectious, and hereditary neuropathic causes; orthopedic, neurosurgical, or neurology assessment of whether the ossification materially compressed the individual nerve
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Traumatic or post-surgical nerve injury at the operative site
Alternative or coexisting entrapment syndromes (cubital tunnel, carpal tunnel, Guyon canal)
Metabolic or toxic neuropathy (diabetes, alcohol, medication-related)
Cervical radiculopathy or plexopathy referred to the limb

evidenceGaps: Imaging or operative documentation of heterotopic ossification (location, extent, relationship to the affected nerve, date); electrodiagnostic confirmation and characterization of the peripheral neuropathy; chronology of the ossification relative to neuropathy onset; documentation of the inciting injury, surgery, or neurologic event; evaluation for alternative or coexisting entrapment sites and for metabolic, toxic, infectious, and hereditary neuropathic causes; orthopedic, neurosurgical, or neurology assessment of whether the ossification materially compressed the individual nerve
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: two independent case reports document heterotopic bone encasing and compressing a peripheral nerve with electrodiagnostic correlation and functional recovery after excision, establishing a reproducible lesion-to-compression association, but the evidence is case-level and narrative-review without incidence denominators and the affected patients carry concurrent trauma, surgery, and alternative entrapment exposures, so the consensus remains NOT_ESTABLISHED with imaging/operative, electrodiagnostic, chronology, and competing-cause requirements; no probability estimate is asserted.
